You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image appear to be a drawing made from chalk?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image as a whole has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing. Fail if it clearly does not have that appearance, including when it shows only an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the appearance cannot be determined.
node.binding: O1: Judge the edited image against the requested outcome of a chalk drawing; supporting evidence does not independently earn completion credit.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image has a soft, grainy, smudged texture and muted colors that make the giraffes and scene appear rendered as a chalk drawing.

fulfillment: The node’s yes rule is too permissive: it treats soft grain, smudging, and muted color as sufficient proof of a chalk-made drawing, although those cues can also describe a filtered or partially stylized photograph. The edited image does show clear chalk-like texture and softened forms, so this is evidence of requested progress—not evidence that no change occurred—but the trace does not establish that the whole scene has become a drawing. Tighten the criterion to assess the overall rendered medium against the source, and distinguish a convincing full-scene chalk drawing from partial chalk effects; do not infer completion from texture cues alone. Preserve the rubric’s partial outcome when progress is visible but completion is not established. Keep the conditional skip for s2 explicitly unobserved rather than treating it as negative evidence. The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth, so use it to investigate the completion boundary rather than force a partial label. No transport or schema failure is shown; the mismatch is semantic criterion calibration.

response.content: {"text":"Revise the binding and criterion so the node judges whether the edited scene as a whole reads as a chalk drawing, not whether it merely has chalk-like texture. Compare with the source and weigh rendered forms and scene-wide medium cues alongside grain, smudging, and muted color; those cues are visible here and indicate real progress, but can also result from a filter and do not alone establish completion. Keep the distinction between no progress, partial progress, and complete fulfillment explicit, and leave completion unresolved when the evidence does not establish the whole-scene transformation. Treat the aggregate reference as a calibration signal, not a forced node label. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated; do not treat an unobserved conditional check as negative evidence."}
